cross_case_findings: Rates use sector deltas times 512 bytes divided by window seconds and 1048576. Logical/physical ratio divides logical write bytes by physical write bytes. Full-pressure percentages divide stall microseconds by window microseconds. Completion ratio is observed completion time divided by baseline time; larger means slower.

Four cases have reader-pinned checkpoint evidence and concurrent copies. WAL growth and zero progress support checkpoint starvation; aggregate disk counters cannot divide traffic between SQLite and the copy or prove device saturation.

Four cases show memory scarcity, swapping and memory full stalls with completion at 2.250000 times baseline. Four other cases show provider 429s and completion at 2.125000 times baseline with little local pressure; retry timelines must confirm remote delay attribution.

Four DELETE-mode cases have busy errors and completion at 1.050000 times baseline. Lock ownership and transaction timing are missing; the busy errors establish contention but do not identify its holder.
Eight cases have baseline completion, ample memory, minimal full stalls and checkpoint progress. These are healthy observed windows, not a capacity ceiling measurement.

Logical/physical write ratios range from 1.000000 to 5.000000 across both healthy and impaired cases. Buffering, coalescing, attribution and writeback timing prevent interpreting these ratios alone as SQLite write amplification. Throughput variation also reflects differing window lengths.
